stops.note: a title of respect, perhaps originally meaning 'father'
in Bengal came to denote an educated native clerk who wrote English
stops.meaning: a native clerk; an educated Bengali gentleman

stops.note: British colonials adopted the word, sometimes with a disparaging tone for stilted English usage
stops.meaning: an Indian clerk; overly formal, bookish English

current_meaning: Historically, a title of respect in South Asia, or (dated, often disparaging) a native clerk fluent in English.
